Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L02_GuidedPractice_Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.09

A student is speaking to the principal to request permission for a school announcement. Which response uses the most appropriate voice and tone?

answer.text: A. Hey, can I do the announcement tomorrow? It will be quick.

feedback.text: This sounds casual for a principal. The message has a clear request, but the voice should be more respectful and formal for the audience.

answer.text: B. I need to make an announcement, so put me on tomorrow.

feedback.text: This sounds demanding. A request should respect the listener and use a tone that makes cooperation more likely.

answer.text: C. Good morning. May I have permission to make a brief announcement tomorrow?

feedback.text: Correct. This response matches the audience by using respectful language, a clear purpose, and a polite tone.

answer.text: D. I might say something tomorrow if that is okay or whatever.

feedback.text: This is unclear and too casual. Audience-aware speaking should state the purpose directly while keeping a respectful tone.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L02_GuidedPractice_Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.09

Which choice best explains why audience matters when choosing tone?

answer.text: A. Audience matters because every speech should sound exactly the same.

feedback.text: This misses the main idea. Speakers adjust tone because different audiences need different levels of formality, detail, and respect.

answer.text: B. Audience matters only when the speaker is giving a long presentation.

feedback.text: This is too limited. Audience affects short comments, questions, discussions, and formal presentations.

answer.text: C. Audience matters because it lets the speaker avoid preparing.

feedback.text: This is the opposite of good communication. Knowing the audience helps the speaker prepare more carefully.

answer.text: D. Audience matters because the speaker should choose language and tone that fit the listener and purpose.

feedback.text: Correct. Audience awareness helps the speaker decide how formal, clear, respectful, and detailed the message should be.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L02_GuidedPractice_Q03

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.05

Which sentence uses academic vocabulary appropriately in a class presentation?

answer.text: A. The stuff proves the thing because it is kind of obvious.

feedback.text: This is too vague for academic communication. Replace unclear words like stuff and thing with precise vocabulary.

answer.text: B. The evidence supports the claim because the data show a clear pattern.

feedback.text: Correct. This sentence uses academic words such as evidence, claim, data, and pattern in a clear way that fits a class presentation.

answer.text: C. Everybody knows this, so I do not need to explain it.

feedback.text: This avoids evidence and explanation. Academic communication should use precise words and support the point clearly.

answer.text: D. My idea is right because I said it strongly.

feedback.text: This focuses on forceful tone instead of academic vocabulary and support. A strong presentation uses precise language and evidence.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L02_GuidedPractice_Q04

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.SPK.01

A student is preparing a short presentation. Which plan best shows logical organization and coherent focus?

answer.text: A. State the topic, explain two supporting points, and end by restating the main idea.

feedback.text: Correct. This plan gives the audience a clear focus, organized support, and a closing statement that reinforces the message.

answer.text: B. Share opinions in the order they come to mind without transitions.

feedback.text: This may confuse the audience. Logical organization uses a clear order and transitions between ideas.

answer.text: C. Start with three unrelated facts, then decide the topic at the end.

feedback.text: This lacks focus. A presentation should begin with a clear topic and keep each detail connected to that topic.

answer.text: D. Use a funny story and skip the evidence because the audience will remember the story.

feedback.text: A story can help, but it should not replace organization and support. The audience still needs a clear point and evidence.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L02_GuidedPractice_Q05

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.09

Read the message: "Your idea makes no sense." Which revision improves the tone for a group discussion?

answer.text: A. Your idea is wrong, and everyone can tell.

feedback.text: This keeps a disrespectful tone. Strong discussion language should address the idea without attacking the person.

answer.text: B. I am not sure I understand your idea yet. Could you explain your reasoning?

feedback.text: Correct. This revision keeps the discussion respectful, asks for clarification, and supports collaboration.

answer.text: C. I will ignore that idea and move on.

feedback.text: This shuts down communication. A better tone keeps the group focused while inviting explanation.

answer.text: D. That idea is confusing, so you should not talk.

feedback.text: This attacks the speaker and discourages participation. Respectful tone helps group members continue learning and contributing.
